title: The Rivets on Jacob Davis's Table and the Letter to Levi Strauss
conflicts: First riveted pair: Davis's 1874 sworn deposition says first week of January 1871 (used); Kelly says 1870 and Wikipedia December 1870 (probably the order date). Origin of the rivet idea: deposition says Davis noticed the rivets himself (used); JMAW says a customer suggested it. Patent rejections: Kelly puts a rejection before the letter, JMAW says the joint application was first rejected as too broad, Clemence says it was reworked several times; story says only 'reworked more than once'. The $68 fee and Annie's refusal rest on one genealogist and are attributed to her.
notes: The core rests on a primary source: Davis's deposition transcript at the National Archives (DocsTeach), plus the patent itself. The letter wording is quoted via America Comes Alive from a Ben Davis Company transcript that is no longer online; the original letter was not seen.
